newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to hover ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to hover ahead of weekend.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to hover on Friday as market participants square positions and await the weekend, brokers said. They said trade was likely to be thin and that arbitrage activity could sway the cash market, but they expected the July options settlement to pass fairly smoothly.
On Thursday, the Nikkei average gained 57.61 points or 0.29 percent to close at 19,754.78 after it briefly touched 19,820.58.
Nikkei 225 September futures ended 80 points higher at 19,780.

"Dealers stepped up buying of blue chips late on Thursday and the focus will be on whether they square positions Friday or hold off until next week," said Isao Takahashi, HSBC James Capel managing director.
Brokers added that index-wise, moves could be small but there was a chance that investors may opt to continue seeking individual shares, especially high-technology issues.
"The yen was around the 112 to the dollar level on Thursday, but that did not discourage buying of high techs," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.
The yen stood at around 113 to the dollar in early Tokyo.

General contractor Aoki Corp was the most heavily traded issue and the largest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo bourse, pressured by concerns over its financial health. Aoki shares tumbled 25 percent or 25 yen to 75, with trade totalling 13.71 million shares.
A spokesman for the medium-sized builder said debts on which the company had provided guarantees totalled 285.2 billion yen as of March 31, 1997, compared with 289.0 billion yen a year earlier.
The debts are held by Aoki affiliates and other firms involved in the contractor's real-estate development projects.
